chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Saeed narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Ruba'i ibn Abdullah from al-Fadl ibn Yasar who said:

Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said to me: When al-Husayn (peace be upon him) moved to Iraq, he entrusted his will, books, and other matters to Umm Salma, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and said to her: When my eldest son comes to you, hand over to him what I have given you. When al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was martyred, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) came to Umm Salma, and she handed over to him everything that al-Husayn (peace be upon him) had deposited with her.

key_terms.أُمِّ سَلَمَةَ: Umm Salma, wife of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Husain entrust to Umm Salma before going to Iraq?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the strategic preservation of Imam al-Husayn’s (a.s) intellectual and spiritual legacy through his mother-in-law, Umm Salma, ensuring its safekeeping during the turbulent post-martyrdom period. It serves as a key evidence for the continuity of authority and knowledge transfer within the Ahl al-Bayt, linking the prophetic household directly to the Imams. The act underscores the importance of familial trust in safeguarding religious texts against potential loss or alteration.
